questions.statement: He has three Ferraris and a huge mansion. He ________ be very rich.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Can't" is for when we are sure something is impossible.
Correct! We use "must" when we are almost certain something is true.
Incorrect. "Might" is for low probability, but here the evidence is strong.
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
Usamos "must" para hacer deducciones cuando estamos casi seguros de que algo es cierto basándonos en la evidencia disponible.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: She just finished a big lunch. She ________ be hungry already!

options.feedback: Correct! "Can't" is used when we are sure something is impossible.
Incorrect. "Mustn't" is for prohibition, not deduction.
Incorrect.
Incorrect. "Couldn't" is usually for past impossibility.

questions.explanation:
Para expresar que estamos seguros de que algo es **imposible** en el presente, utilizamos el modal "can't".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "Where is my phone?" - "I'm not sure. It ________ be in your backpack."

options.feedback: Incorrect. The speaker is "not sure".
Correct! "Might" (or "could") is used for possibilities when we aren't certain.
Incorrect.
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
Usamos "might", "may" o "could" cuando algo es posible pero no estamos seguros de ello.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Don't eat those mushrooms! They ________ be poisonous.

options.feedback: Incorrect. We don't know for sure they are poisonous.
Correct! "Could" expresses a possibility or risk.
Incorrect.
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
"Could" funciona de manera muy similar a "might" en las deducciones presentes, indicando una posibilidad teórica o real de que algo ocurra.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The lights are off and there is no car in the driveway. They ________ be at home.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The evidence suggests they are out.
Correct! The evidence makes it very unlikely they are there.
Incorrect.
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
Nuevamente, cuando la evidencia apunta fuertemente a que algo es falso o imposible, el modal correcto es "can't".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He speaks with a very strong paisa accent. He ________ be from Antioquia.

options.feedback: Correct! The accent is strong evidence of his origin.
Incorrect.
Incorrect.
Incorrect. While similar, "must" is better for logical deduction.

questions.explanation:
La deducción lógica basada en señales culturales (como un acento específico) se expresa con "must" si la probabilidad es muy alta.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses a **logical deduction** of impossibility?

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a prohibition (rule).

options.text: That can't be Carlos; he is in London right now.
options.feedback: Correct! This is a logical conclusion based on a fact.
Incorrect. This is advice.
Incorrect. This is lack of ability.

questions.explanation:
Es vital para un estudiante B1 distinguir entre los diferentes usos de los modales. "Mustn't" nunca se usa para deducciones, solo para reglas o prohibiciones.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
**Speaker 1:** "It might rain."
**Speaker 2:** "It must be raining."

What is the difference?

options.feedback: Incorrect.
Correct! "Must" shows high certainty; "might" shows low certainty.

options.text: They both mean the same thing.
options.feedback: Incorrect.

options.text: Speaker 1 is talking about the past.
options.feedback: Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
Los modales de deducción forman una escala de certeza: Must (95-100%) > Might/Could/May (30-50%) > Can't (0-5%).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Listen! Someone is playing the guitar. It ________ be our neighbor; he practices every day at this hour.

options.feedback: Correct! High probability deduction.
Incorrect.
Incorrect. "Must" is stronger here.
Incorrect. We need a modal to show deduction.

questions.explanation:
Podemos usar modales seguidos de "be + -ing" (aunque aquí sea simple) para deducir acciones que están ocurriendo en el momento.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "You have been working for 12 hours without a break. You ________ be exhausted!"

options.feedback: Correct! This is the most logical conclusion.
Incorrect. Illogical after 12 hours of work.
Incorrect. It's more than just a possibility.
Incorrect. This would be a recommendation ("Deberías estar cansado"), which sounds strange.

questions.explanation:
En el nivel B1, el estudiante debe evaluar el contexto para elegir el grado de certeza correcto. Después de un esfuerzo largo, el cansancio es una conclusión casi segura.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: There are wet footprints on the floor, but it's not raining outside. Which deduction is the most logical?
questions.context: Evaluating a guess in a mystery scenario.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The context says it's not.

options.text: Someone might have just stepped out of the shower.
options.feedback: Correct! Logical alternative possibility.
Incorrect. Contradicts the footprints.
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
Resolver "misterios" cotidianos requiere evaluar múltiples posibilidades y descartar las que contradicen los hechos conocidos.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"A new student arrived today. He has a very large camera and is taking photos of everything in the school. He doesn't speak much Spanish yet."
What can we deduce?

options.text: He might be a foreign exchange student interested in photography.
options.feedback: Correct! Combines all the evidence into a logical possibility.

options.text: He must be the school principal.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Principals usually speak Spanish and don't take photos of everything.
Incorrect. He has a large camera.

options.text: He will be a famous actor in the future.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Too speculative.

questions.explanation: Sintetizar información para llegar a una conclusión razonable es una habilidad clave evaluada mediante el uso de modales de deducción en el nivel B1.
